turn.user_message: Show me how we’ll know it worked
turn.context: Discharge sample conversation, turn 9 (playbook §4: only the measures with a number or a goal; new ones marked new).

text: We will watch a short list of numbers, week by week. Where you already gave me a number, that is where we start. Why these:
bullets: They measure the wait itself, not how busy people are, so a busy week cannot hide a slow one.
They start from your own numbers, so progress is measured against you, not other hospitals.
Nothing tracks some of them today. Those are marked new, and the trial’s first week gives their starting number.
chat.invite: That is all five parts. Shall I put them into a plan, starting with a short trial?
chat.note: Measure the wait, not the effort.

points.label: Decisions made on the evening round

prompts: Yes, put it into a plan
Who reports these numbers each week?
What counts as a good result?
chat.pointer: Pick a dial to see how it is measured. Dashed dials have no number yet.

sheets.title: Hours from ready to home
sheets.text: From the doctor saying the patient can go, to the patient leaving. Counted for every patient, reported every week, ward by ward.
sheets.entry: Who could record the leaving time?

sheets.title: Home by 10 AM
sheets.text: The share of each day’s patients who have left by those times. The first week of the trial sets the starting number.
